reference_opening.argument: This video is scam content because it promotes making money through BitClub-branded Bitcoin mining and presents displayed account earnings as income generated by miners. It guides viewers through a participation and withdrawal flow involving a Bitcoin payout address, a withdrawal amount, and an emailed security PIN. The example is not completed, so it does not establish that Bitcoin was paid, that the displayed balance was genuine, or what happened to submitted information.

citations.quote: How to Withdraw My Earnings on Bitclub Network
once we have worked or our miners have been generating income for us we will see where you can withdraw

opening.argument: Judge this as an example, not proof of a payout or a promise that viewers will earn one. The speaker expressly says the transfer will not be made because the account lacks enough money. That qualification matters: the video shows a procedure while leaving its outcome unverified. Even the account figure is presented as a small available amount, not evidence of a completed withdrawal. The defensible reading is a limited demonstration whose speaker does not claim to have proved that the process succeeds.

citations.quote: I'm not gonna do it because you don't have enough money this is nothing more that an example
as maximum I have here 0.66 equivalent to 8 dollars

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution is right that the speaker attributes income to miners, but that does not turn the unfinished example into evidence of a successful payout or a guaranteed return. Its own point that no transfer is completed cuts against treating the walkthrough as a verified earnings claim. The speaker explicitly marks the attempted transfer as an example and says it will not be performed.

citations.quote: once we have worked or our miners have been generating income for us we will see where you can withdraw
I'm not gonna do it because you don't have enough money this is nothing more that an example

true_side_reply.rebuttal: Acknowledging that this particular transfer is only an example does not retract the broader pitch. The speaker still describes miners as generating income, and the closing card urges viewers to make money mining Bitcoin. The absence of a completed payout limits what the video proves about payment; it does not erase its promotion of mining returns.

citations.quote: once we have worked or our miners have been generating income for us we will see where you can withdraw

opening.argument: The video's immediate task is operational: it starts from the account back office, locates the wallet and withdrawal area, explains where a Bitcoin address goes, and walks through the emailed PIN step. Its title likewise promises instructions on withdrawing, not a return calculation. The speaker stops short of requesting the transfer. A judge should distinguish teaching an existing user how an interface works from establishing that the underlying earnings are real.

citations.quote: How to Withdraw My Earnings on Bitclub Network
this time we will see how to withdraw money
we would copy and we would take to here we would paste we would save
Now we want to add a pin of four digits that we will have to insert here.
I'm not gonna do it because you don't have enough money this is nothing more that an example

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution's account of the wallet address, amount, and PIN accurately describes a withdrawal tutorial. Those steps do not themselves show a viewer being asked to invest or establish that a payment was made. The speaker's miner-income language supplies context for why someone would use the screen, but the demonstrated action remains an unfinished account procedure.

citations.quote: once we have worked or our miners have been generating income for us we will see where you can withdraw
I'm not gonna do it because you don't have enough money this is nothing more that an example

true_side_reply.rebuttal: The procedural format is real, but it is embedded in a mining-income pitch. The speaker presents the displayed account amount as generated by the mining business, while the site shows a mining-pool offer and the closing card promotes making money mining Bitcoin. An incomplete withdrawal demonstrates neither payment nor legitimacy; it also does not make the surrounding earnings promotion merely neutral instruction.

citations.quote: what has been generated in this account by the mining business

opening.argument: What is actually demonstrated is a service account's Bitcoin wallet workflow. The speaker describes setting a payout address and requesting a withdrawal, while the screen shows an available balance and a withdrawal form. The video does not show this request being completed, and the cited walkthrough supplies no guaranteed rate of return or instruction to hand the speaker a password or PIN. The presence of an account balance and withdrawal controls is not, by itself, proof of a deceptive transaction.

citations.quote: any withdrawal would go here to this wallet
I'm not gonna do it because you don't have enough money this is nothing more that an example

rebuttal.rebuttal: The prosecution treats the displayed earnings and payout-address steps as part of the mining offer. But the quoted miner statement does not specify a guaranteed return, and the withdrawal screens do not establish that the speaker receives the address or security PIN. Its caution that no payment is proven is warranted; the same evidentiary limit prevents these screens alone from proving deception.

citations.quote: once we have worked or our miners have been generating income for us we will see where you can withdraw

true_side_reply.rebuttal: A guaranteed rate or credential handoff is not necessary to recognize what this video promotes. The site displays a mining-pool offer, the speaker calls the account amount income generated by mining, and the closing card explicitly urges making money mining Bitcoin. The withdrawal tutorial reinforces that claimed earning opportunity even though this example does not complete a payment.
